open_points.subject: concurrency review coverage of Room records in backups
open_points.text: A18 says a backup “holds every record but the agent sessions (M06)”, but A21’s concurrency affected-model list is “M01, M04, M05, M06, M09, M10, M11” and omits M03 Room even though backup snapshots include rooms.
open_points.question: Does A21’s concurrency review cover M03 and concurrent room creation during a backup, or is the affected-model list intentionally exhaustive and excluding it?
options: The affected list is exhaustive, so M03 was not reviewed despite being copied.
“backup snapshots taken while transactions go on” implicitly covers M03, and the model list is non-exhaustive.
M03 must be added explicitly to the affected list.
open_points.default_guess: Treat backup snapshot coverage as including M03 and add it explicitly to the affected list.

witness.initial: A full Registry instance has an active project and no room R; a daily backup run is due.
events: The backup begins its store snapshot.
The owner concurrently adds room R and that transaction commits.
outcomes: M03 is within the reviewed concurrency scope, so evidence must establish that the backup contains either all or none of R’s transaction.
M03 is excluded by A21’s affected list, so the security review requires no room-specific snapshot evidence even though A18 copies the room.
witness.observer: The security reviewer and the later test author see whether this race must be covered.

open_points.subject: scope of non-overlapping backup runs
open_points.text: A18 says “Runs never overlap” and A21 relies on “non-overlapping runs”, but neither text says whether this excludes only two runs in one process, all runs for one store, or all processes and instances using the same backup location.
open_points.question: Across what boundary must backup runs be mutually exclusive, and what happens if two valid Registry processes or instances use the same backup location?
options: Only runs scheduled by one process cannot overlap.
All runs for the same Registry store cannot overlap, including across process replacement.
Any runs sharing a backup location cannot overlap, even when they back up different stores.
Sharing a backup location between instances is invalid configuration and must be refused.
open_points.default_guess: Require the backup location to be exclusive to one instance and treat non-overlap as applying across every process using that instance’s store and backup location.

witness.initial: Two Registry instances on different hosts have distinct stores but valid configurations resolving to the same shared backup directory; neither text expressly refuses this configuration.
events: Both processes observe their respective 03:00 UTC crossing.
Instance P creates its temporary backup file.
Instance T starts step one, which removes every file under the temporary prefix.
outcomes: Non-overlap is global to the shared location, so one run waits or is skipped and P’s temporary file is untouched.
Non-overlap is only per process or instance, so T removes P’s in-progress file and one or both runs fail or produce different kept-backup sets.
witness.observer: The owner sees different diagnostics and a different newest kept backup; a later restore may have a different backup available.

open_points.subject: verification of non-overlapping backup runs
open_points.text: A21 rule 1 says each applicable category is supported by its decisions’ required tests and now expressly relies on A18’s “non-overlapping runs”, but A18’s required tests contain no test that starts or attempts two backup runs concurrently.
open_points.question: What required evidence verifies the non-overlap property on which the changed concurrency review relies?
options: A new concurrency test must attempt two scheduler/run starts and prove only one executes.
The normative sentence alone is considered sufficient even though every listed required test can pass in an implementation that permits overlap.
An existing required test is intended to cover non-overlap and must be identified.
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit test that races two eligible run starts and verifies that only one run manipulates backup files.
